rationale: Walking trajectories point in both directions across older exercise participants and Friedreich ataxia cohorts. Both contexts use cointerventions or active comparators, and the oil's cold-press grade and Parkinson effect remain unverified. FORCES has planned gait results in sarcopenia.

One Friedreich ataxia crossover reported slightly improved timed speech during safflower periods without a significant comparative effect on specific features. The ALS trial gives composite bulbar scores only. Neither study measures intelligibility in Parkinson with verified cold-pressed oil.

Whole-oil rodent movement measures vary with spontaneous activity, novelty, and training. Safflower flavonoid extract studies in Parkinson models test a distinct preparation. Parkinsonian bradykinesia after cold-pressed oil remains unmeasured.

Lower novelty exploration after developmental safflower diets and improved depression-like behavior after a purified safflower pigment are endpoint-limited and exposure-limited leads. Apathy-specific evidence for cold-pressed seed oil in Parkinson remains unavailable.
An ALS trial's safflower comparator has composite scores that include swallowing. Item-level changes, exact grade and Parkinson dysphagia evidence remain open.

A Parkinson meal patent reports outcomes from formulas that contain canola and sunflower oil. The safflower recipes have no observed outcomes. The search found no refined-safflower evidence with daily levodopa OFF time.

Static balance was largely unchanged in Friedreich ataxia and reached a measurement ceiling in an older-adult exercise trial. FORCES has a planned balance test but no results. Reactive Parkinson balance under cold-pressed safflower remains open.

Ataxia joint mobility and muscle strength tests did not measure resistance to passive movement in Parkinson. Safflower flavonoid models do not establish a culinary seed-oil effect and one original report has an unresolved corrigendum.
The Friedreich ataxia trial reported five falls on USP safflower and seven on active RT001. Falls were adverse events and a baseline fall rate, cold-press grade and Parkinson population are absent.
